sites.name: Wildcat Ridge
sites.quote: The outcrop is a horizontally layered, fine-grained, and well-sorted sedimentary rock; it is a sulfate-bearing coarse mudstone ... Thus, this rock has high potential for biosignature preservation.
sites.why_category: Layered, fine-grained mudstone that NASA says has high biosignature-preservation potential.
sites.look_for: Thin flat layers in fine-grained, light-toned rock; sulfate minerals; the same layers above and below the sampled spot.
sites.position_source: core site lat/lon from the PDS Initial Report

sites.name: Amalik (Enchanted Lake member)
sites.quote: The outcrop is a horizontally layered, fine-grained, and well-sorted sedimentary rock; it is an olivine-bearing coarse mudstone ... likely deposited on to the floor of a lake.
sites.why_category: Layered, fine-grained lake-floor mudstone near the base of the delta.
sites.look_for: Fine layering; the light-toned, laminated Kaguyak sandstone about 1 m below; altered olivine grains.
sites.position_source: core site lat/lon from the PDS Initial Report

sites.name: Hidden Harbor (Yori Pass member)
sites.quote: The outcrop is a horizontally layered, fine-grained, and moderately sorted sedimentary rock; a sulfate-bearing fine sandstone
sites.why_category: Layered and fine-grained (fine sandstone); the report rates its biosignature-preservation potential as high.
sites.look_for: Light-toned layered rock on its natural surface; sulfate cement.
sites.position_source: core site lat/lon from the PDS Initial Report

sites.name: Skinner Ridge (Lower Rockytop member)
sites.quote: Skinner Ridge lies at the base of ~6.5 vertical meters of exposed sedimentary rock layers of Rockytop ... The outcrop is a horizontally layered, medium-grained clastic sedimentary rock
sites.why_category: Medium-grained (not fine) sandstone at the base of a 6.5 m exposed stack of delta layers: shows how the deposits changed.
sites.look_for: The 6.5 m stack of Rockytop layers above; grain size changes between layers.
sites.position_source: core site lat/lon from the PDS Initial Report

sites.name: Berea / Melyn (Upper Fan, delta top)
sites.quote: Medium-grained sandstone with occasional clasts up to ~ 3 mm, likely deposited in a fluvial setting. Although layering is apparent in the cored outcrop
sites.why_category: River (fluvial) sandstone on top of the delta: the river stage that followed the lake deposits below.
sites.look_for: Layering in the outcrop; small pebbles up to ~3 mm; carbonate alteration.
sites.position_source: core site lat/lon from the PDS Initial Report

sites.name: Delta-top boulder field
sites.quote: some of them were likely sourced from outside of Jezero crater. These boulders were washed down a river ... the boulders may have come from up to tens of kilometers away
sites.source: NASA blog 'Look at All Those Boulders!' (2023-04-17) https://science.nasa.gov/blog/look-at-all-those-boulders/
sites.why_category: Boulders NASA says were likely carried in by rivers from outside the crater: matches the rubric exactly.
sites.look_for: Rounded boulders of different rock types; compare with the layered rock below.
sites.position_source: rover position on sol 754 = last waypoint on or before sol 754 (M20_waypoints.json); the boulders are in the camera view, not exactly at this point -> waypoint 37_1798 (sol 753)
